content.text:
I submitted **index 142** (Bi 0.167, Cu 0.226, V 0.607). It gave the highest photocurrent of the three compositions I measured: **3.04×10⁻⁵ A**. I used all 3 merit measurements and 3 of the 5 XRD scans.

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 105 | 0.43 / 0.23 / 0.35 | 3.7×10⁻⁷ |
| 54 | 0.11 / 0.29 / 0.61 | 2.82×10⁻⁵ |
| 142 | 0.17 / 0.23 / 0.61 | 3.04×10⁻⁵ |

- **Where the good region is:** the vanadium-rich corner (V about 0.6) gave about 80 times more photocurrent than index 105, which is close to a 1:1 Bi:V ratio but contains 23% Cu.
- **What XRD suggests:** samples in that corner look like a mixture of two phases:
  - One phase's peaks match what I expect for monoclinic BiVO4. It is strongest in the Bi-richer samples 54 and 147.
  - A second phase has a strong peak at Q 1.744 Å⁻¹ and dominates index 13, the most Cu-rich of the three XRD samples. From its composition it may be a copper vanadate such as CuV2O6, but I didn't confirm that. I couldn't open the reference phase list because it was too large to read here and shell access was turned off.
- **Why 142:** moving from 54 to more Bi and less Cu at the same vanadium level raised the photocurrent a little.

With only three measurements, the true best composition may still be unmeasured. The model's top suggestions, such as index 23 (Bi 0.18, Cu 0.22, V 0.60), are close to 142 but were never measured.
